CAN_ADMIN_KEY.description: PutKeyPolicy or CreateGrant (can grant itself decrypt); ScheduleKeyDeletion.

CAN_ADMIN_SG.description: Can change security-group rules (network exposure). Targets the SG (was the instance).

CAN_ASSUME.description: sts:AssumeRole is allowed by the role's trust policy and, where needed, the caller's identity policy (same-account root trust, cross-account, wildcard). Replaces CAN_ASSUME_CROSS.

CAN_ASSUME_WEB_IDENTITY.description: AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity admitted by the trust policy; props.admits = any | pattern | specific.

CAN_DECRYPT.description: kms:Decrypt (key-policy-first evaluation). GenerateDataKey* alone is CAN_ENCRYPT.

CAN_ESCALATE.description: Self-escalation, or modification of a principal the source can already act as (closure, engine.md §4.6); evidence.chain lists the edge ids.

CAN_MODIFY_PERMISSIONS_OF.description: Put*/Attach*Policy, CreatePolicyVersion, SetDefaultPolicyVersion or boundary changes on another principal. Closure input: becomes CAN_ESCALATE when the target is reachable.

CAN_REACH_NODE_IMDS.description: The pod can reach the node's IMDS (hop limit, hostNetwork); Fargate excluded. evidence.weight_extra adds 0-2 by hop limit.

CAN_READ_SECRET.description: secretsmanager:GetSecretValue (BatchGet only with it). Metadata actions give no edge.

CAN_TAKEOVER.description: Credential or trust takeover of another principal: CreateAccessKey, Create/UpdateLoginProfile, UpdateAssumeRolePolicy, AddUserToGroup. Self is excluded.

CAN_UPDATE_CODE.description: lambda:UpdateFunctionCode: code execution as the execution role.

CAN_WRITE_SECRET.description: Update, put, delete, rotate or change the policy of the secret.

CLUSTER_ROLE.description: EKS control-plane service role; workloads never get it.

EC2_FULL_ACCESS.description: ec2:* on the instance: user-data change plus stop/start gives code execution.

FULL_ACCESS.description: s3:* (identity policy or same-account bucket-policy grant).

HAS_POLICY.description: Managed policy attached to the principal (ARN-keyed).

INSTANCE_ROLE.description: Code on the instance gets the instance-profile role's credentials from IMDS. ARN-resolved; the dashboard's name-matched copy is removed.

IRSA_BRIDGE.description: IRSA: the annotated role trusts this service account through the cluster's OIDC provider.

IS_ADMIN_EQUIVALENT.description: The principal is admin-equivalent (ADMIN-001), so reaching it means reaching the account admin.

NODE_ROLE.description: Node instance role, reachable through node IMDS.

PUBLIC_INBOUND.description: Reachable from the internet (security groups, routes, NACLs, scheme, endpoint access). INTERNET_FACING is folded into props.igw_routed.

RUNS_AS.description: The pod mounts the service-account token (automount on).

SECRET_ENCRYPTED_BY.description: The secret's KMS key (default aws/secretsmanager resolved).

SERVICE_CAN_ASSUME.description: The trust policy admits an AWS service principal (PassRole candidates, confused-deputy checks).

SSRF_TO_IMDS.description: Public, running instance with IMDSv1 and a role: SSRF can read role credentials. Always conditional. Re-aimed from instance→role (dashboard) to anonymous→instance.

USES_ROLE.description: The compute resource runs as the role (Lambda execution role, ECS task role, stack service role, job role). The ECS execution role is EXECUTION_ROLE.

evaluation_gaps.detail: The report predates _coverage.json: denied or failed collection cannot be told apart from empty data.
Identity policies of external principals are not visible; cross-account edges are conditional.
IAM was collected with the per-entity (d13c215) layout: no policy versions, no identity providers, boundaries and tags may be missing
Resource control policies are unknown (membership unknown)
Service control policies are unknown (membership unknown)
Condition values known only at request time (source IP, MFA, tags in the request) are not evaluated; such decisions are conditional.
Session policies passed at AssumeRole time can only narrow permissions and are not modelled.

findings.description: This role is administrator-equivalent: its effective permissions allow every action on every resource. Its 67 individual privilege-escalation and dangerous-permission findings are summarised here.
findings.remediation: Treat this principal as an account administrator: limit who can use it (trust policy, group membership, credentials), require MFA, and replace broad grants (Action:* or iam:*) by the permissions it needs.
findings.title: Administrator-equivalent principal

findings.description: Every pod running as service account apps/apps-sa can assume arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/demo-irsa-west1, which is administrator-equivalent in AWS: compromising one such pod compromises the account.
findings.remediation: Restrict the role to the permissions the workload needs, and scope its trust policy to this service account (exact sub and aud conditions).
findings.title: Service account can assume an admin IAM role through IRSA (apps/apps-sa, cluster demo-eks-west1)

findings.description: Web identity provider arn:aws:iam::111122223333:oidc-provider/oidc.eks.eu-west-1.amazonaws.com/id/LDHIOKBHIGNLJHNLLOFDEFCEJMOFIAFN can assume 'demo-irsa-west1'; oidc.eks.eu-west-1.amazonaws.com/id/ldhiokbhignljhnllofdefcejmofiafn:sub missing.
findings.remediation: Require the provider's audience (<host>:aud) and an exact subject (<host>:sub), e.g. repo:<org>/<repo>:ref:refs/heads/main for GitHub or system:serviceaccount:<ns>:<sa> for EKS.
findings.title: Role 'demo-irsa-west1' trusts eks identities (any subjects)

findings.description: In region eu-west-1, no trail covers this region; this is an old report, which listed trails without shadow / organization trails and lost every trail's status (F-045, F-047): re-collect to confirm.
findings.remediation: Create a multi-region trail (or an organization trail) that logs management events, with log file validation and a protected destination bucket.
findings.title: No CloudTrail trail is verified logging region eu-west-1

findings.description: The Kubernetes API endpoint of cluster demo-eks-west1 (eu-west-1) is publicly accessible from 0.0.0.0/0. Authentication is still required, but any leaked kubeconfig, token or mapped IAM credential is usable from anywhere, and API-server vulnerabilities are exposed.
findings.remediation: Disable public endpoint access, or restrict publicAccessCidrs to known administration networks.
findings.title: EKS cluster demo-eks-west1 has a public API endpoint open to the internet

findings.description: SSM parameter '/demo/eu-west-1/db_password' has type 'String' (plaintext) but its name has a credential word as a whole token. Anyone with ssm:GetParameter on it reads the value in plaintext, with no KMS gate.
findings.remediation: Migrate the parameter to type SecureString (KMS-encrypted).
findings.title: Parameter '/demo/eu-west-1/db_password' looks like a secret but is stored as a plaintext String
